clue.text: A bishop among drunken actors and circus performers?

indicators.note: something placed among others goes in with them, so the pair of letters joins the group of letters
a drunken person staggers about, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman finds himself among a rowdy, tipsy troupe of actors and circus folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The A and the bishop's B join the letters of actors, and the whole lot is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobats are performers of tumbling and balancing feats, a staple act of the circus ring; the question mark flags the playful phrasing.

clue.text: A male do, crazy and fashionable

indicators.note: something crazy is out of its right mind, so these letters fall into a disordered arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A party for men only turns out wild yet stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' here is a party, a British use; in the wordplay it simply supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A la mode is a borrowed French phrase meaning in the current style or trend.

clue.text: Reversible component of machine

indicators.note: a reversible word can be read backwards without changing, which describes a word spelt the same both ways

parts.note: the turning part of a motor, which reads the same in either direction

explanation.surface: A machine part that can be turned round and fitted either way.
explanation.walkthrough: ROTOR reads the same backwards, so 'Reversible' describes the word, not the machine part.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine such as a motor, turbine or helicopter.

clue.text: Supports drinking and excessive cordiality?

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
lapping is drinking with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Fans cheering and drinking together, with a bit too much bonhomie.
explanation.definitionFit: Backslapping is hearty, showy friendliness, slapping people on the back, often more than sincere.

clue.text: Story about second-rate item of furniture

indicators.note: about means around, so the story wraps around the grade letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
B grade is second rate, below A

explanation.surface: An account of a shoddy piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is a standard piece of furniture with a flat top on legs.

clue.text: Map book has bit of Texas torn out unfortunately

parts.note: the first letter of the state's name

explanation.surface: Sadly, someone has ripped the Texas page out of the road atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection expressing regret, used just as unfortunately is at the start of a sentence.

clue.text: Opponent of modernisation did wrong breaking into instrument

done wrong means done incorrectly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters of did, rearranged
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A reactionary smashes his way into a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The Luddites were early 19th-century English workers who smashed new textile machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A Luddite is anyone hostile to new technology, named after those machine-wrecking workers.

clue.text: Child participating in adventurous programme

indicators.note: participating in something means being part of it, so the word is inside the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A youngster is taking part in an outdoor activity course.
explanation.walkthrough: SPROG is informal British slang for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is a jokey colloquial term for a young offspring or kid.

clue.text: A cur's taken on manoeuvres, bad-tempered

explanation.definitionFit: Cantankerous describes someone grumpy, quarrelsome and difficult, a synonym for irritable.

clue.text: Greek house's storage space?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of Athens or the ancient region around it
second meaning: the room under the roof

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Greek home has a place to keep things.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic is both the adjective for ancient Athens and its dialect, and the noun for a loft room under a roof.

clue.text: Edge of country accommodating a pupil in dormitory?

parts.note: a border is the edge of a country
taken as written

clue.text: Rower initially on a river

parts.note: the first letter of on
taken as written

clue.text: Ex-PM in wrongdoing, needing good protection

clue.text: Capture parent going wild

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Duty to get horse into physical condition

explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage was historically a tax levied on ships' cargo by the ton, a customs duty.

clue.text: Trendy act certainly

parts.note: in means fashionable
a deed is an act

clue.text: It's crazy, going up over a long time for Mars

parts.note: mad means crazy
ages is a long time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' is not the planet but the verb, to spoil; 'over' places the first piece above the second in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to spoil or harm, so mars and damages are the same verb form.
